analysis: All three changed files are test-only: ModelLoadEvictionAndAdmissionTests.swift (new test at head lines 90-114), NemotronSuperManagedSlotTests+LoadGate.swift (an onShutdown hook added to the fixtures at head lines 36-49, plus three new tests at 267-332), and StandaloneServerModelAdmissionTests.swift (one new test, patch hunk lines 517-537). No production source, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization or cache-storage code changes, so no security regression is visible in the supplied evidence. The new tests assert behavior that touches TB-007 and T-028/T-041. Parked, retained free KV segments (and the buffer pool) are released before an idle model is evicted or a load is refused. Pre-accept counts those segments as reachable. The StandaloneServer headroom gate releases retained KV backing even when eviction is disallowed. These behaviors reduce residual KV memory and do not widen any trust boundary. The tests use only in-memory stubs (RetainingEngineStub, ParkedBytesRecorder, inert bridges) and temporary directories under FileManager.temporaryDirectory. They write no real keys, consumer data or at-rest cache artifacts, and they do not touch the SSD prefix cache, the KEK or the HMAC lookup tags. The `@Sendable` onShutdown closure added to the fixtures defaults to a no-op, so existing tests are unaffected. The production implementations that these tests exercise (evictUntilAvailable, evictUntilNemotronSuperFits, fastAdmissionReject, ensureMemoryHeadroomForLoad) are not in the supplied diff. I could not verify them, so the integration pass should confirm that the release-before-evict logic exists and that it releases or zeroes parked memory without leaking it across tenants. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a flaw.
